stem: Why did the authors expect infants to look longer at the old item rather than the new one at test?
choices: Items were seen once, briefly, so not fully habituated
Old items were repeated until infants habituated
New items came from an unfamiliar category
Old items were paired with a sound at encoding
answer: Items were seen once, briefly, so not fully habituated

stem: How many infants contributed usable awake fMRI data to the hippocampal subsequent memory study?
label: Results · sample

stem: At the group level, how did infants' looking at old versus new items at test compare?
choices: A strong preference for the old item
A strong preference for the new item
No reliable preference for the old item
An old-item preference in older infants alone
answer: No reliable preference for the old item
label: Results · group behaviour

stem: How did overall behavioural familiarity preference differ between infants younger and older than 1 year?
choices: It was higher in the older group
It was higher in the younger group
It did not differ between age groups
It reversed to a novelty preference in the younger group
answer: It did not differ between age groups
label: Results · age and behaviour

stem: Across all 26 infants, how did whole-hippocampus BOLD activity at encoding relate to a later familiarity preference for that item?
choices: Greater for items later looked at longer
Lower for items later looked at longer
No relation in the full sample
Greater for items later looked away from
answer: Greater for items later looked at longer
label: Results · subsequent memory effect

stem: Which hippocampal subdivision showed a significant subsequent memory effect in infants?
label: Results · anterior vs posterior

stem: Was the infant subsequent memory effect significantly larger in the posterior than the anterior hippocampus?
choices: No, the difference was not significant
Yes, but only in the older infants
answer: No, the difference was not significant

stem: Which confounds did control analyses rule out as explanations of the infant hippocampal subsequent memory effect?

stem: Did hippocampal encoding activity track the overall strength of infants' test preference when old- and new-item preferences were pooled?
choices: No, it was specific to old-item preferences
Yes, more strongly than for old-item preferences
Yes, but only for scene items
answer: No, it was specific to old-item preferences
label: Results · specificity

stem: Splitting infants at the median of their average familiarity preference, where was the hippocampal subsequent memory effect reliable?
choices: In infants with a lower average familiarity preference
In infants with a higher average familiarity preference
Equally in both halves of the sample
In neither half once split by median
answer: In infants with a higher average familiarity preference

stem: Which design feature did the authors flag as complicating the null effect in younger infants?
choices: Fixed stimulus duration despite age differences in encoding time
Mixing three stimulus categories within one session

answer: Fixed stimulus duration despite age differences in encoding time

stem: What did exploratory analyses of the test trials tentatively suggest about the infant hippocampus?

Posterior hippocampus may support retrieval in older infants
Hippocampus is suppressed during retrieval at all ages
Orbitofrontal cortex alone supports retrieval in older infants
answer: Posterior hippocampus may support retrieval in older infants
